entry.title: OPD Odata extraction using CDC and filter on initial load
entry.content:
Hello!

As you might know, the closing of ODP-RFC connections for 3rd party application has forced us to look at alternatives to our data ingestion into Azure ADF and/or databricks. 

Datasphere is the alternative, but we're also considering other options, one of which is OData ODP extraction.

At this point in time, we have quite a few big tables, with over 1 billion records in the tables.

According to many documentations, OData and ODP supports $filter, however, we noticed a behavior we're not sure how to avoid.

We are using CDS views with annotations @analytics: {dataExtraction: {enabled: true,delta.changeDataCapture: {automatic: true} so utilizing the native S4HANA 2023 on-prem functionality. 

Upon initializing the delta via OData with odata:track-changes header and $filter to avoid loading 1b records that we already have in target system, a new subscription is created in ODQMON with initial delta with filter. Using the provided deltatoken for next delta request, it actually results in yet another initial delta with filter being the exact opposite of the first filter. So we end up in the first request asking for 20 records, and second request gives us the remaining 999.9999.980 mio that we try to avoid.

 

How would you go about delta initializing with CDC without needed to fetch the whole tables?

entry.title: Deep entity $expand throws "Method X_GET_ENTITY not implemented" in Gateway service
entry.content:
I have a custom OData service with a deep entity structure — a main entity set with several navigation properties, one of which has its own sub-navigation (e.g. MainSet(Key)?$expand=NavA,NavB/NavC).

GET_EXPANDED_ENTITYSET is implemented and works fine when I request the full list with $expand. But as soon as I request a single record by key plus $expand, I get:

/IWBEP/CM_MGW_RT/021
Method 'X_GET_ENTITY' not implemented in data provider class

Why does this happen, and what's the correct fix?

---

Answer:

The Gateway framework routes single-record reads (URL with keys) through GET_ENTITY, and multi-record reads through GET_ENTITYSET / GET_EXPANDED_ENTITYSET. Implementing only the "set" variant handles list requests but not Set(key1='..',key2='..')?$expand=... calls — those always go through GET_ENTITY.

Fix: implement the corresponding _GET_ENTITY method in your DPC_EXT class, mirroring the logic already in GET_EXPANDED_ENTITYSET, but return a single deep structure into er_entity instead of a table into et_entityset.

Also verify that any sub-level navigation (NavA/NavC) is modeled as a navigation inside NavA's own structure/DDIC type — not as a second top-level navigation off the main entity. Otherwise the expand path won't resolve even after adding GET_ENTITY.

entry.title: OData URL looks correct but returns 404 — turned out to be case sensitivity in EntitySet/key names
entry.content:
My OData GET request keeps returning 404 even though the URL looks correct and the service is active in /IWFND/MAINT_SERVICE:

/sap/opu/odata/sap/MY_SRV/MyEntitySet(Key1='X',Key2='Y')

/IWFND/ERROR_LOG doesn't show anything obviously wrong. What's a systematic way to debug this?

---

Answer:

Before touching backend code, check $metadata first — it's the fastest way to rule out casing/naming issues:

/sap/opu/odata/sap/MY_SRV/$metadata

In one recurring case, the actual generated EntitySet name was myEntitySet (lowercase first letter) instead of MyEntitySet, and one key property was lowercase (bukrs) instead of the expected Bukrs. OData is case-sensitive, so a URL that "looks right" will still 404 if it doesn't match the exact name in the model.

Debug order that saves time:
1. Hit $metadata directly — confirm exact EntitySet Name= and Key PropertyRef Name= casing.
2. If $metadata itself 404s, the service isn't activated/registered — check /IWFND/MAINT_SERVICE and SICF.
3. If $metadata works but the entity call still fails, fix the URL to match the exact casing from the XML.
4. Update the CASE ls_key-name. logic in your DPC_EXT class to match the exact (case-sensitive) key names from metadata — a mismatch here causes silent SELECT misses even after the URL is fixed.

entry.title: How to handle omitted fields (partial updates) in OData v2 CREATE_DEEP_ENTITY without clearing data?
entry.content:
Hello,

We have developed a custom OData v2 service (zmdg_businesspartner_srv) to accept complex, deep payloads from MuleSoft.

The problem:
When the external system sends a partial update, it omits unchanged fields to save bandwidth. 

SFDC JSON:
{
"FirstName":"Richard",
"LastName":"Millard"
}

Informatica JSON
{
"FirstName":"Richard",
}

In SAP OData structure we'd built the structure using SFDC basis. When Informatica sends it only sends FirstName. CREATE_DEEP_ENTITY requires an HTTP POST, SAP Gateway assigns ABAP initial values to any omitted fields. Our backend ABAP code overwrites the existing "Last_Name" in SAP with a blank.

My Question:
1. Is there a standard framework method to detect exactly which fields were passed in a CREATE_DEEP_ENTITY POST request?
2. How to not set any value when the field is omitted? 

Any advice or code snippets would be gently appreciated!

entry.title: API_MATERIAL_STOCK_SRV sandbox returns 401 - gateway/backend auth mismatch
entry.content:
I'm getting a consistent 401 Unauthorized calling the API_MATERIAL_STOCK_SRV sandbox API (A_MatlStkInAcctMod entity), and I've isolated it to something on the sandbox backend, not my credentials.

Request:

 
GET /s4hanacloud/sap/opu/odata/sap/API_MATERIAL_STOCK_SRV/A_MatlStkInAcctMod?$filter=Material eq 'CH_C_104'&$format=json
Header: APIKey: <my key>

Response: 401 Nicht autorisiert (SAP's own HTML error page)

Response headers include:

 
www-authenticate: Basic realm="SAP NetWeaver Application Server [EJS/100][alias]"
sap-authenticated: false
sap-system: EJS

This suggests the public API gateway is accepting the request, but the backend NetWeaver system it forwards to is expecting HTTP Basic Auth instead of the API key — a gateway-to-backend mismatch, not an invalid key.

What I've already ruled out:

  • Confirmed the API key is current via "Show API Key" in account settings
  • Regenerated a fresh API key — same result
  • Tested via curl directly and via the API's own "Try Out" tool on this page — same 401 both ways
  • API status on its overview page shows "Active," not deprecated

Timing: the issue started around when the API's page showed "Last Modified: 10 Sep 2026, Version 1.1.0" — possibly related to that update. It's now been several days with no change.

Has anyone else hit this, or is there a known issue with this sandbox after the recent version update? Happy to share my API key ID or further details if useful for troubleshooting.

Update: I tested a sibling entity in the same API product, A_MaterialSerialNumber, and it returns 200 successfully through the same key and the same "Try Out" tool. Only A_MatlStkInAcctMod specifically returns 401. This confirms it's isolated to this one entity's backend, not the API product, key, or subscription as a whole
